analysis.title: International Market Intelligence | Morning Briefing (October 19, 2026)
key_insights: Tech weakness is inducing a broadening rotation. US and NDX are outperforming this morning after last week's Tech selloff and Friday's vol spike.
EU equities are supported by the broadening rotation. Weekend developments (Russia/Ukraine tensions, protests in France) are likely contributing to today's unwind.
Oil is lower after Trump waived energy sanctions and struck a diesel deal with Russia.

EUR is taking a notable hit on politics, fiscal concerns and geopolitics. FX strategy flags EUR as having taken the brunt of USD buying and as the shortest currency across their metrics. Downside is somewhat capped, with less than one fifth of EUR/USD puts struck below 1.10 in October.

Last week's broadening was mostly a rotation induced by Tech weakness. EU vs US relative performance bounced off lows. JPM held the view that the technical setup for broadening had improved but needed a catalyst to extend.

Rates were the key support last week. It is unclear whether lower yields came from risk-off/safe-haven rotation or from concern about Tech/capex spending (evidenced by CoreWeave), which reduces yield pressure. Positioning is another likely driver: the Flows & Liquidity MOMO signal reverted materially from early October's extreme shorts.

Aggregate positioning is neutral, but Positioning Intel flags multi-strat de-grossing as close to the worst in the past 2 years. The backdrop was fragile: gross still high long-term, 3m combined Tech flows near multi-year highs, and NDX long vs RTY short futures skews extreme.
Positioning extremes persist in AI Core Revenue, Semis vs Software, and Utilities (heavily under-owned).
Korea weakness: buybacks slowing, foreign selling, trend-following investors substantially reduced exposure, long-only appetite contingent on vol moderating, and fragile retail sentiment.

Credit strategists see the magnitude of hyperscaler spread widening as overdone. Debt is up $117bn YTD but average ratings improved modestly. The moves reflect selection/dispersion, not indiscriminate HG exposure reduction.

Week ahead: Fed and ECB enter blackout, China macro data, Merz at the Invest in Germany Summit, UK CPI, NVDA GTC, global S&P PMIs. Key earnings include NFLX, TSLA, META, IBM, SAP, EU Luxury and Banks.

JPM is tactically bullish on global equities. The regional preference is long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) vs EU. The US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation, and Asia has pockets of both.
The broadening trade can return, more clearly in US than EU. European earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but EGB spread stability is needed for conviction in EU.

EM monetization: bullish on EM on global macro strength, AI capex tailwinds, and diversification via commodities, policy easing scope and political catalysts. EM has recovered over 9% of its drawdown since the end-July bottom. Country-relative trades are preferred.
Positioning Intelligence weekly wrap: HF performance drawdown accelerated to -2.1% MTD globally (from -0.8%). Eq L/S -2.3% MTD, Quants -1% to -2%, Multi-Strats -2%, APAC -3.8% MTD.

The current setup echoes 2023 more than 2018. A stronger YTD cushion (HFs about +6% YTD, MXWD about +13%, SPX about +14%) supports an eventual stabilization and a 4Q rally as more likely than not, unless earnings or data deteriorate.
